title: Short Stuff: Battle of Itter Castle
summary: Short Stuff episode on the Battle of Castle Itter (Schloss Itter) in the Tyrolean region of Austria, in the final days of World War II. Hosts cover the castle's history as a VIP prison annex of Dachau, the SS threat as the war wound down, the escape of a Yugoslavian handyman who reached American troops, the rescue party led by German defector Sepp Gangl and Captain Jack C. Lee with a tank under Major John T. Kramer, the siege by Waffen SS, Gangl's death by sniper, and the arrival of the American tanks that ended the fighting. Lee later became an old man and received the Distinguished Service Cross.
topics: end of World War II in Europe

segments.title: Opening banter
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck introduce the short episode on the Battle of Castle Itter, noting its cinematic story and the unusual mix of Germans, Americans, French and others fighting the Nazis.

segments.title: Castle history and VIP prisoners
segments.summary: The castle has stood since the 13th century and was taken over by the Nazis after the 1938 annexation of Austria. In 1943 it became part of Dachau as a VIP prison for high-value prisoners of war, including two French generals and two former French prime ministers, held as possible hostages.
topics: French prisoners in World War II

segments.title: Collapse of Germany and SS threat
segments.summary: In early May 1945 Germany was collapsing; Hitler and Mussolini were dead and surrender was imminent. Some SS units wanted to surrender while others planned to fight to the end, leaving the castle prisoners fearing for their lives.
topics: end of World War II in Europe

segments.title: Edward Vitter's arrival and suicide
segments.summary: Edward Vitter, the commandant of Dachau, arrived at the castle in May 1945 after escaping the Allies and ordering the execution of about 2,000 prisoners. He shot himself in the heart and then in the head.

segments.title: Yugoslavian handyman seeks help
segments.summary: After the castle guards left, the prisoners were trapped. A Yugoslavian handyman escaped to find American troops, reached them, and Major John T. Kramer agreed to send a small detachment of tanks.

segments.title: Sponsor break
segments.summary: Mid-episode break; the hosts pause the story before the rescue party is introduced.

segments.title: Rescue party forms
segments.summary: The cook of the castle went for help and found German major Sepp Gangl, a defector who had broken with the SS. Gangl joined with Captain Jack C. Lee and his tank, the Besotten Jenny, plus members of an all-Black company, and the group moved toward Castle Itter, arriving about twelve hours before the siege.

segments.title: Siege of the castle
segments.summary: Waffen SS forces arrived and attacked. The rescue group knocked out the tank parked in front of the main gate. The defenders had pistols, rifles and machine guns from the armory, but ran low on ammunition as the Nazis used an 80mm gun against the walls. Gangl was killed by a Nazi sniper and Lee became the de facto commander.

segments.title: Defensive plan and keep
segments.summary: Lee planned to hold the defenders in the castle keep and funnel the SS through a narrow passage to pick them off. Hosts discuss Gangl's death and the grim odds.

segments.title: Relief by American tanks
segments.summary: Kramer's tank column arrived, attacked the Nazis from the rear, and the battle ended almost immediately. Lee later recounted Kramer's arrival; Lee lived to an old age and was awarded the Distinguished Service Cross.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: Hosts wrap up, calling the story movie material, and close the Short Stuff episode.
